question: A microbiologist is involved in research on the emergence of a novel virus, X, which caused a recent epidemic in his community. After studying the structure of the virus, he proposes a hypothesis: Virus X developed from viruses A and B. He suggests that viruses A and B could co-infect a single host cell. During the growth cycles of the viruses within the cells, a new virion particle is formed, which contains the genome of virus A; however, its coat contains components of the coats of both viruses A and B. This new virus is identical to virus X, which caused the epidemic. Which of the following phenomena is reflected in the hypothesis proposed by the microbiologist?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Co-infection of host cell by viruses A and B -> Formation of new virion particle with genome of virus A and coat components of both viruses A and B -> Emergence of virus X with a mixed coat -> Phenotypic mixing -> 95%

CHAIN: Co-infection of host cell by viruses A and B -> Genetic reassortment leading to the formation of a new virus with components from both viruses A and B -> Emergence of virus X -> Genetic reassortment -> 90%

CHAIN: Co-infection of host cell by viruses A and B -> Formation of new virion particle with genome of virus A and coat components of both viruses A and B -> Emergence of virus X with a mixed coat -> Antigenic shift -> 85%
analysis: The hypothesis proposed by the microbiologist describes a phenomenon where a new virus is formed through the combination of genetic material from two different viruses during co-infection of a host cell. This process results in the creation of a novel virus with a genome from one virus and coat components from both parent viruses.
